intro: Competitive surfing is judged: in short heats, surfers ride as many waves as they like, and a panel of judges scores each ride from 0 to 10. Only each surfer's two best waves count. Because the ocean is unpredictable, wave selection and the right-of-way system — priority — are as important as manoeuvres. The International Surfing Association (ISA) governs Olympic surfing; the World Surf League (WSL) runs the professional tour.
inThirtySeconds: Heats last around 20–35 minutes with two to four surfers.
Each wave is scored 0–10; your two best waves make your heat total out of 20.
The surfer with priority has the right to any wave they choose.
Dropping in on someone else's wave is interference and costs heavily.
objective: Finish in the advancing positions of each heat by posting the highest two-wave total.

facts.environment: Ocean breaks (and some artificial wave pools)

scoring.label: Wave score
scoring.detail: Judges score each ride; the highest and lowest of five scores are discarded and the rest averaged.

scoring.label: Heat total
scoring.detail: Sum of a surfer's two best wave scores.

bodies.name: International Surfing Association
bodies.scope: World governing body; runs Olympic qualification

rules.title: Judging criteria
rules.summary: Judges reward commitment and difficulty, innovative and progressive manoeuvres, combinations of major manoeuvres, variety, and speed, power and flow.
rules.body: The emphasis of each criterion can change with the conditions: big, hollow waves favour tube rides, while softer waves reward aerial manoeuvres. A scale guides scores — for example 8.0–10.0 is 'excellent'.

rules.title: Two best waves
rules.summary: Surfers can ride many waves, but only their two highest scores count.
rules.body: This means a surfer behind can come back with one big score. Commentators talk about the 'needs' score — what a surfer must score to take the lead.
rules.example: Waves scored 7.5, 6.2 and 3.0 give a heat total of 13.70.

chapters.title: Priority and interference
chapters.summary: The right of way in the water.

rules.title: Priority
rules.summary: In most heats, a priority order decides who may catch the next wave. The surfer with priority can take any wave; others may only paddle for it if the priority surfer doesn't.
rules.body: When a surfer catches a wave or paddles for one and misses, they drop to the lowest priority. Priority is signalled by coloured lights or discs on the beach.

rules.title: Interference
rules.summary: Hindering a surfer who has the right of way — for example dropping in on their wave — is an interference.
rules.body: The penalty typically reduces the offender's scores: one of their best two waves is halved or removed, depending on the rule book. Repeated interference can lead to disqualification from the heat.

fouls.name: Drop-in
fouls.description: Taking off on a wave in front of a surfer with right of way.

fouls.name: Paddling interference
fouls.description: Blocking another surfer's paddle for a wave.

fouls.name: Exceeding wave limit
fouls.description: Riding more waves than allowed in the heat.

flow.title: Heat start
flow.description: A horn and lights signal the start.

flow.title: Wave selection
flow.description: Surfers use priority to pick the best waves.

flow.title: Last minutes
flow.description: Trailing surfers chase the needed score.

flow.title: Advance
flow.description: Top finishers move to the next round.

positions.name: Regular foot
positions.role: Rides with the left foot forward.

positions.name: Goofy foot
positions.role: Rides with the right foot forward.

field.name: Competition area
field.dimensions: A marked zone of the break, defined by flags on the beach
field.surface: Ocean waves (beach, reef or point breaks)
notes: Priority display visible from the water
Contest waiting periods allow organisers to pick the best swell

glossary.definition: Riding inside the hollow curl of a wave.
Launching the board above the lip of the wave.
Catching a wave in front of someone with right of way.

funFacts: Surfing made its Olympic debut at Tokyo 2020, held in 2021.
The Paris 2024 Olympic surfing event was held in Teahupo'o, Tahiti — about 15,000 km from Paris.
